Generate a synthetic firm panel for public release using only random numbers.
Do not use the actual data used in the analysis.
The distributions and parameters below are chosen for this computational example and do not guarantee replication of the empirical results or the validity of the model.

Save `sample_size_tb` and `sample_growth_tb`, with the same columns, types, and units as the actual data, in both `qs2` and `parquet` formats in `../Zipf_law_board_replicate_simulation/`. Saving in `parquet` format requires the R package `arrow`.
The QMD files in 02–11 change only the input board path; their computational procedures are those used in the actual analysis.

## 1 Setup and generation parameters

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(pins)
theme_set(theme_light())

# Use the same random sequence when rendering again.
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
seed <- 20261019L
set.seed(seed)

# 06_Girard.qmd requires positive growth rates through rank 60,000.
# Using too small a sample causes the final validation to stop execution.
n_firms <- 300000L
birth_years <- 1940:2020
simulation_years <- min(birth_years):max(birth_years)
years <- 2005:2020 # Observation period saved for analysis
# Parameters for log sales at birth only; set separately from shock_shape / shock_scale for growth.
initial_log_sale_location <- log(2e5) # Location of log sales (median sales are 200 million yen)
initial_log_sale_sd <- 1.0
initial_log_sale_scale <- initial_log_sale_sd / sqrt(2)
annual_drift <- 0
shock_shape <- 0.55
shock_scale <- 0.06

# Do not read from or write to the original board for actual data.
board <- board_folder("../Zipf_law_board_replicate_simulation", versioned = FALSE)
dir.create("graph", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("latex", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## 2 Synthetic firm attributes and sales panel

Firm IDs are sequential numbers prefixed with `SIM`. Firms are born in every year from 1940 to 2020.
Allocate 300,000 firms as evenly as possible across the 81 establishment years, so annual firm counts differ by at most one.
Construct four-digit industry codes by selecting the first two digits from 01–99 and the last two from 00–99.
Include synthetic industries subject to exclusion so that the industry exclusions in the analysis code can be applied without modification.

Let $B_i$ denote firm $i$'s establishment year. Independently generate the natural logarithm of sales at birth, measured in thousands of yen, from a common Laplace distribution regardless of establishment year.

$$L_{i,B_i}\sim\operatorname{Laplace}(m_0,s_0),\qquad m_0=\log(2\times10^5),\qquad s_0=1/\sqrt{2}.$$

Set the location $m_0$ using `initial_log_sale_location` and the standard deviation of 1 using `initial_log_sale_sd`.
Set the Laplace scale to `initial_log_sale_scale`, calculated as the standard deviation divided by $\sqrt{2}$.
The density is $f(x)=\exp(-|x-m_0|/s_0)/(2s_0)$.
Median sales at birth are 200 million yen.
Generate initial log sales independently of annual growth rates.
Do not add a growth shock to sales in the birth year; from the following year onward, add a signed Weibull log growth rate once per year.

$$g_{it}=\mu+S_{it}W_{it},\qquad W_{it}\sim\operatorname{Weibull}(a,b),\qquad P(S_{it}=1)=P(S_{it}=-1)=1/2.$$

$$L_{it}=L_{i,B_i}+\sum_{u=B_i+1}^{t}g_{iu},\qquad t\geq B_i,\qquad \mathrm{sale}_{it}=\exp(L_{it}).$$

In the birth year, the empty sum is defined as zero.
Here, $\mu=0$, $a=0.55$, and $b=0.06$. Initial log sales and growth shocks are independent, as are growth shocks across firms and years.

Generate the growth process year by year from 1940 through 2020.
Save observations for 2005–2020 in `sample_size_tb` for use in analyses 02–11.
For example, log sales in 2005 for a firm born in 1940 include the value at birth and 65 growth increments from 1941 to 2005.

```{r}

# Assign firms to every establishment year, then randomize the assignment to IDs.
firm_tb <- tibble(
  id = sprintf("SIM%07d", seq_len(n_firms)),
  birth_year = as.numeric(sample(rep(birth_years, length.out = n_firms))),
  ind_class = sprintf(
    "%02d%02d",
    sample(1:99, n_firms, replace = TRUE),
    sample(0:99, n_firms, replace = TRUE)
  ),
  # Use signed exponential draws to generate Laplace values at birth independently of growth.
  birth_log_sale = initial_log_sale_location + initial_log_sale_scale *
    sample(c(-1, 1), n_firms, replace = TRUE) * rexp(n_firms, rate = 1)
) |>
  mutate(birth_date = sprintf("%04d0101", as.integer(birth_year)))

# Firms have no sales before birth.
log_sale <- rep(NA_real_, n_firms)
n_growth_steps <- integer(n_firms)
annual_tables <- vector("list", length(years))
for (this_year in simulation_years) {
  newborn <- which(firm_tb$birth_year == this_year)
  log_sale[newborn] <- firm_tb$birth_log_sale[newborn]

  # Add one year of growth to existing firms each year from the year after birth through 2020.
  continuing <- which(firm_tb$birth_year < this_year)
  if (length(continuing) > 0L) {
    shock <- sample(c(-1, 1), length(continuing), replace = TRUE) *
      rweibull(length(continuing), shape = shock_shape, scale = shock_scale)
    log_sale[continuing] <- log_sale[continuing] + annual_drift + shock
    n_growth_steps[continuing] <- n_growth_steps[continuing] + 1L
  }

  active <- which(firm_tb$birth_year <= this_year)
  # Verify that no growth was added in the birth year and exactly one increment was added each subsequent year.
  stopifnot(
    all(n_growth_steps[active] == this_year - firm_tb$birth_year[active]),
    all(log_sale[newborn] == firm_tb$birth_log_sale[newborn]),
    all(is.finite(log_sale[active])),
    all(is.na(log_sale[firm_tb$birth_year > this_year]))
  )

  # Calculate growth histories before 2005 as well, but save only the years used in the analysis.
  if (this_year %in% years) {
    annual_tables[[match(this_year, years)]] <- firm_tb[active, ] |>
      transmute(
        id,
        date = sprintf("%04d12", this_year),
        month = 12,
        sale = exp(log_sale[active]),
        year = as.character(this_year),
        birth_date,
        ind_class,
        birth_year
      )
  }
}
sample_size_tb <- bind_rows(annual_tables)
rm(annual_tables, log_sale, n_growth_steps, firm_tb)
gc(verbose = FALSE)

sample_size_tb |> slice_head(n = 10)
```

## 3 Growth

Here, calculate $g_{i,t,s}=\log(\mathrm{sale}_{it})-\log(\mathrm{sale}_{is})$ for ten annual periods and nine periods starting in 2010.
Growth is `NA` for periods in which sales are unavailable before establishment.

```{r}

# Define ten annual periods and nine periods starting in 2010, in the original order.
growth_pairs <- tibble(
  post = c(2020:2011, 2012:2020),
  pre = c(2019:2010, rep(2010, 9))
) |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("g_%02d_%02d", post %% 100, pre %% 100))

growth_wide <- sample_size_tb |>
  filter(year > 2000) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = id, names_from = year, values_from = sale)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(growth_pairs))) {
  growth_wide[[growth_pairs$label[i]]] <-
    log(growth_wide[[as.character(growth_pairs$post[i])]]) -
    log(growth_wide[[as.character(growth_pairs$pre[i])]])
}

growth_tb <- growth_wide |>
  select(-starts_with("20")) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("g_"), names_to = "year", values_to = "growth") |>
  filter(!is.nan(growth), !is.infinite(growth))

```

Create `sample_growth_tb` with firm attributes (establishment year and industry) and corresponding sales levels (beginning and end years).

* Collect and join each firm's `birth_year` and `ind_class` in `firm_attributes`  
  Use the attributes from the firm's first appearance in `sample_size_tb`, without restricting to 2010.

* Add variables `pre_sale` and `post_sale`  
  For example, when year = g_13_10, post_year = 2013 and pre_year = 2010.  

```{r}

firm_attributes <- sample_size_tb |>
  select(id, birth_year, ind_class) |>
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)

sales <- sample_size_tb |> select(id, year, sale)

sample_growth_tb <- growth_tb |>
  left_join(firm_attributes, by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    pre_year = str_c("20", str_sub(year, 6, 7)),
    post_year = str_c("20", str_sub(year, 3, 4))
  ) |>
  left_join(
    sales |> rename(pre_sale = sale),
    by = c("id" = "id", "pre_year" = "year")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    sales |> rename(post_sale = sale),
    by = c("id" = "id", "post_year" = "year")
  ) |>
  select(-pre_year, -post_year)

# Save the data after the validation below.
sample_growth_tb |> slice_head(n = 10)

```

```{r}
board |> pin_write(sample_size_tb, "sample_size_tb", type = c("qs2", "parquet"))
board |> pin_write(sample_growth_tb, "sample_growth_tb", type = c("qs2", "parquet"))

```
